6The gradient

Board heading: The Gradient

Define

So:

Explanation (added)

The formula from the theorem is a dot product in disguise: one vector holds the partials and the other holds the direction. The vector of partials gets a name because it comes up again and again, and it depends only on and the point, not on the direction. Once you have at a point, every directional derivative there is one dot product away. Stewart §14.6 Definition 8 and Equation 9.

12The tangent plane

Definition

The tangent plane to surface at to be the plane containing with normal

This plane has equation:

Explanation (added)

Every curve in through has its tangent vector perpendicular to , so all those tangent vectors lie in one plane. That plane is what “tangent plane” means. The equation is the point-normal equation of a plane from §12.5, with replaced by the three partials. It needs , or there is no normal to use. Stewart §14.6 Equation 19.

What a typical exam question looks like
  1. Direction given by an angle. Find at a point where makes a given angle with the horizontal. Use exact values of and (Section 5).
  2. Direction given by a vector that isn't unit. Divide by its length first, find at the point, and take the dot product (Section 8).
  3. Fastest change. Find the maximum rate of change of at a point and the direction in which it occurs: and (Section 10).
  4. Tangent plane to a surface that isn't written as a level surface. Rewrite it as , find at , and write the plane (Section 13).
  5. Explain or prove. Show why using (Section 4), or why the maximum is using (Section 10).
